response_text:
Design Document — LLM-Based User Profile System from Browser Behavioral Signals
Target product: AI assistant embedded in Microsoft Edge
Goals: infer interests, preferences, and context from browser behavioral signals and summarize into a 5-layer profile that the assistant reads synchronously to personalize responses.

Contents
1) Full Profile Schema (5 layers) — exact fields, types, examples, relations
2) Generation Pipeline — inputs, LLM prompt templates, triggers, merge strategies
3) Storage & Serving Architecture — technology, caching, read/write paths
4) LLM Summarization Pipeline — batching, model choices, example prompt, parsing, failure handling
5) Evaluation Framework — offline/online metrics, A/B test design, privacy checks
At the end: open questions and tradeoffs called out.

SECTION 1 — FULL PROFILE SCHEMA (JSON / pseudo-JSON)
Notes:
- Profiles contain ONLY derived attributes (no raw event storage).
- Each user has one Profile document keyed by user_id.
- Profile size target ~2KB average.

Top-level structure (high-level)
{
  "user_id": "string",                 // internal key
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "last_updated": "ISO8601 timestamp",
  "layers": {
    "L1_identity": { ... },
    "L2_preferences": { ... },
    "L3_interests": { ... },
    "L4_world_context": { ... },
    "L5_interest_cards": [ ... ]
  },
  "metadata": { ... }                  // e.g., consent flags, quality scores
}

Layer L1 — Identity (Monthly)
Purpose: stable personal & professional attributes and communication style.
Update cadence: Monthly (or triggered by explicit signals like editing profile).

Fields:
{
  "occupation": { "value": "string", "confidence": 0.0-1.0, "derived_from": ["domains","bookmarks"] },
  "expertise_domains": [ { "topic": "string", "confidence": 0.0-1.0 } ],   // up to N=8
  "preferred_communication_style": { "tone": "concise|detailed|friendly|formal", "examples": ["I like bullets"], "confidence": 0.0-1.0 },
  "native_language": { "value": "string", "confidence": 0.0-1.0 },
  "timezone": { "value": "IANA/Olson zone", "confidence": 0.0-1.0 },
  "last_verified": "ISO8601 timestamp"
}

Example:
" L1_identity": {
  "occupation": { "value": "software engineer", "confidence": 0.92, "derived_from":["visited job sites","LinkedIn-like patterns"] },
  "expertise_domains": [ {"topic":"web development","confidence":0.88}, {"topic":"cloud infra","confidence":0.55} ],
  "preferred_communication_style": { "tone":"concise", "examples":["prefer bullet lists","avoid long background"], "confidence":0.75 },
  "native_language": {"value":"en-US","confidence":0.98},
  "timezone":{"value":"America/Los_Angeles","confidence":0.99},
  "last_verified":"2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"
}

Relation to other layers:
- L1 is the stable backbone used to interpret L2-L5 (e.g., occupation informs interest interpretation).
- Changes here should be conservative (high threshold to update).

Layer L2 — Preferences (Weekly)
Purpose: behavioral presentation preferences and persistent content-level preferences.
Update cadence: Weekly (or explicit user edits).

Fields:
{
  "content_length_preference": {"value":"short|medium|long","confidence":0.0-1.0, "rationale":"visited summaries vs full articles"},
  "format_preference": {"value":"bullet|paragraph|step-by-step|code-snippets","confidence":0.0-1.0},
  "formality": {"value":"formal|neutral|informal","confidence":0.0-1.0},
  "topics_to_avoid": [ {"topic":"string","reason":"sensitivity|irrelevance","confidence":0.0-1.0} ],
  "privacy_display_pref": {"value":"minimal|full|explainable","confidence":0.0-1.0},
  "communication_channel_pref": {"value":"chat|email|doc|code","confidence":0.0-1.0},
  "last_updated":"ISO8601"
}

Example:
" L2_preferences": {
  "content_length_preference":{"value":"short","confidence":0.86},
  "format_preference":{"value":"bullet","confidence":0.72},
  "formality":{"value":"neutral","confidence":0.9},
  "topics_to_avoid":[ {"topic":"celebrity gossip","reason":"irrelevant","confidence":0.95} ],
  "privacy_display_pref":{"value":"explainable","confidence":0.6},
  "communication_channel_pref":{"value":"chat","confidence":0.8},
  "last_updated":"2026-04-01T07:00:00Z"
}

Relation:
- Guides how the assistant formats responses when using interests/context. Lower update frequency than L3.

Layer L3 — Interests (Daily)
Purpose: active interest clusters; the assistant uses these to bias retrieval and suggestions. Contains confidence and recency-weighted activity scores.
Update cadence: Daily (or on relevant event spikes).

Fields:
{
  "clusters": [
    {
      "id": "string (hash/topic-id)",
      "label": "string (short label)",
      "keywords": ["keyword1","keyword2"],
      "examples": [ {"url":"string","title":"string","timestamp":"ISO8601"} ],
      "score": 0.0-1.0,               // normalized interest strength
      "last_activity": "ISO8601",
      "decay_half_life_days": number
    }
  ],
  "global_confidence": 0.0-1.0,
  "last_computed": "ISO8601"
}

Example:
" L3_interests": {
  "clusters":[
    {"id":"c1","label":"Generative AI","keywords":["GPT","LLM","fine-tuning"],"examples":[{"url":"https://arxiv.org/..","title":"Scaling laws","timestamp":"2026-04-07T19:01:00Z"}],"score":0.93,"last_activity":"2026-04-07T19:01:00Z","decay_half_life_days":7},
    {"id":"c2","label":"Electric Cars","keywords":["EV","Tesla","charging"],"examples":[{"url":"https://news.com/ev","title":"New EV model","timestamp":"2026-04-05T09:00:00Z"}],"score":0.45,"last_activity":"2026-04-05T09:00:00Z","decay_half_life_days":14}
  ],
  "global_confidence":0.87,
  "last_computed":"2026-04-07T20:00:00Z"
}

Relation:
- L3 is the operational core for personalization. L2 shapes which clusters are favored/avoided (e.g., topics_to_avoid negative bias). L1 provides context (occupation influences cluster labels and weights).

Layer L4 — World Context (Daily)
Purpose: snapshot of what the user is actively working on (projects, recent searches, urgent topics).
Update cadence: Daily and event-triggered for high-activity changes.

Fields:
{
  "active_projects": [
    {
      "project_id":"string",
      "title":"string",
      "description":"string",
      "related_topics":["string"],
      "last_updated":"ISO8601",
      "urgency_score":0.0-1.0
    }
  ],
  "recent_searches": [ {"query":"string","timestamp":"ISO8601","clicks":[{"url":"string","title":"string"}]} ],
  "recent_news_topics": [ {"topic":"string","source":"string","timestamp":"ISO8601"} ],
  "working_hours_pattern": {"start_time":"HH:MM","end_time":"HH:MM","confidence":0.0-1.0},
  "last_snapshot":"ISO8601"
}

Example:
" L4_world_context": {
  "active_projects":[ {"project_id":"p-42","title":"Q2 Product Launch","description":"Preparing marketing copy and competitor analysis","related_topics":["product marketing","competitor research"],"last_updated":"2026-04-07T17:35:00Z","urgency_score":0.81} ],
  "recent_searches":[ {"query":"best pricing for SaaS","timestamp":"2026-04-07T16:20:00Z","clicks":[{"url":"https://example.com/pricing","title":"SaaS pricing"}]} ],
  "recent_news_topics":[ {"topic":"chip shortage","source":"nytimes","timestamp":"2026-04-07T09:00:00Z"} ],
  "working_hours_pattern":{"start_time":"09:00","end_time":"17:30","confidence":0.9},
  "last_snapshot":"2026-04-07T20:00:00Z"
}

Relation:
- L4 is ephemeral context to bias responses in-session (e.g., assistant suggests items related to active_projects). L3 supplies topic clusters; L2 may instruct assistant how to present suggestions.

Layer L5 — Interest Cards (Event-triggered; transient)
Purpose: short-lived, high-signal cards created by specific trigger patterns — used for immediate, contextual suggestions (expire after 48 hours).
Update cadence: event-triggered.

Card schema (array of cards):
[
  {
    "card_id":"string",
    "trigger_type":"pattern_name",
    "title":"string",
    "summary":"string (1-2 lines)",
    "linked_topic_id":"string (L3 cluster id or free text)",
    "priority": 0-100,
    "created_at":"ISO8601",
    "expires_at":"ISO8601",
    "signals":["page_visit","highlight","search_term"],
    "evidence": [ {"type":"url","value":"string","timestamp":"ISO8601"} ],
    "actions":[ {"action_type":"suggest_reply","payload":"..."} ],
    "consumed": boolean
  }
]

Example card:
{
  "card_id":"card-20260407-001",
  "trigger_type":"rapid_search_spike",
  "title":"Preparing slides on Generative AI",
  "summary":"User ran 7 searches in 1 hour about prompt engineering and opened three tutorial pages.",
  "linked_topic_id":"c1",
  "priority":85,
  "created_at":"2026-04-07T19:15:00Z",
  "expires_at":"2026-04-09T19:15:00Z",
  "signals":["search_queries","page_visits"],
  "evidence":[ {"type":"search_query","value":"prompt engineering best practices","timestamp":"2026-04-07T18:59:00Z"} ],
  "actions":[ {"action_type":"suggest_summary","payload":"Offer 3-slide summary on prompt engineering"} ],
  "consumed": false
}

Relation:
- L5 references L3 clusters and L4 context. L5 is intentionally transient and prioritized for immediate personalization. Cards do not persist beyond expiry except for audit logs (if allowed by privacy rules).

Metadata/top-level fields
{
  "consent": { "profile_enabled": boolean, "layers_enabled": { "L1":true,... }, "consent_timestamp":"ISO8601" },
  " pii_blocklist": ["email","phone","full_name"] (automatically detected & redacted),
  "profile_deletion_flag": boolean,
  "quality_scores": { "L1":0.0-1.0, "L2":..., "L3":..., "L4":..., "L5":... }
}

SECTION 2 — GENERATION PIPELINE (per layer)
General principles:
- Each layer has a defined signal set, LLM summarization template, update trigger, and merge strategy.
- All LLM calls return structured JSON mapped to the schema — strict parsers & validators applied.
- Confidence thresholds decide whether to accept updates; if below threshold, mark as tentative.
- No raw behavioral data is stored — only event-derived summaries and metadata (counts/timestamps, not raw content).

Layer L1 — Identity
- Input:
  - Aggregated signals over 30+ days: frequently visited domains (domain categories), bookmarks (derived categories), long-duration dwell on professional sites (e.g., LinkedIn), repeated query patterns, explicit profile edits.
  - Only aggregated counts/taxonomy used (no raw visited pages).
- LLM summarization prompt (template):
  - System: "You receive aggregated behavioral signals (domain categories, counts, aggregated snippets) describing a user's long-term activity. Produce a compact JSON describing occupation, expertise domains, preferred communication style, native language, and timezone. Use conservative inference and include confidence 0-1 and brief evidence notes (categories only). Do not hallucinate PII."
  - Input: structured aggregated signals.
- Trigger:
  - Time-based: monthly re-compute.
  - Event-based: user explicitly edits identity or aggregated signal crosses strong threshold (e.g., new verified LinkedIn bookmark).
- Merge strategy:
  - Weighted merge with decay: new L1 candidate is merged via confidence-weighted update; only overwrite if new_confidence > existing_confidence + delta (delta e.g., 0.15). Also record last_verified and provenance.
  - Mostly conservative — prefer not to flip occupation frequently.

Layer L2 — Preferences
- Input:
  - Aggregated UI interactions (preferred article lengths clicked, whether user opened full article or left after summary), formatting signals (copy patterns, highlight frequency), explicit settings.
- LLM summarization prompt:
  - System: "From weekly aggregated signals about content consumption and UI interactions, infer presentation preferences in JSON (length, format, formality, topics_to_avoid). Base decisions on observed behaviors; cite evidence as categories or counts. If insufficient signal, set confidence low."
- Trigger:
  - Weekly scheduled job, or explicit user setting change event.
- Merge strategy:
  - Overwrite per-field when new_confidence >= old_confidence OR if explicit user-edits occur (explicit overrides auto-inferred).
  - If new_confidence < old_confidence, produce a tentative suggestion stored in metadata but not applied.

Layer L3 — Interests
- Input:
  - Last 7 days of derived signals: domain categories counts, search queries aggregated (not raw queries), clicked result categories, highlights/annotations categories, time-of-day-weighted visits.
  - Signals are pre-processed to topic-candidates via a lightweight topic classifier (non-LLM) producing candidate topic tokens + scores.
- LLM summarization prompt (more detail below — full example provided in Section 4).
- Trigger:
  - Daily scheduled job (nightly), and event-triggered for activity spikes (e.g., > N visits on a topic within M hours).
- Merge strategy:
  - Weighted merge with recency: existing clusters decay per their half-life; new clusters are added; for overlapping clusters use a merge-by-Jaccard on keywords with confidence-weighted averaging of scores. If the LLM indicates a rename/merge, perform merge with human-defined rules to prevent accidental overwrites.
  - Persist examples (one or two) per cluster (URLs / titles) but only storing derived metadata (no raw full-text).

Layer L4 — World Context
- Input:
  - Recent searches (aggregated), active tab set snapshots, time-series of visits in last 24–72h, task-switching patterns.
- LLM summarization prompt:
  - System: "Given recent aggregated signals (search categories, tabs open, and visit durations), summarize the user's current focus as active projects, their short descriptions and urgency, plus recent searches. Output JSON per schema. Use caution: do not infer PII."
- Trigger:
  - Daily, plus real-time event-trigger when a large context change is detected (e.g., user opens > 5 tabs matching a topic within 20 minutes).
- Merge strategy:
  - L4 is mostly ephemeral; overwrite the L4 snapshot when recomputed. Keep a short timeline history (e.g., last 7 snapshots) for audit/trending but limited to derived metadata only.

Layer L5 — Interest Cards (Event-triggered)
- Input:
  - Near-real-time derived signals (count/velocity patterns): rapid search spikes, repeated visits to similar resources, highlights & copy events, bookmarks in a short window.
- Trigger patterns (concrete):
  1) Rapid Search Spike: user issues >= 5 queries matching a topic cluster within 60 minutes and clicks >=3 results in that cluster => create card "Research sprint on [topic]".
  2) Long Dwell + Copy: user spends > X minutes on a long article (scroll depth >80%) and performs copy/annotation events => create card "User reading & extracting on [topic]".
  3) Task Window Opened: user opens 4+ tabs with pages strongly matching a cluster and switches among them frequently within 30 minutes => create card "Preparing materials for [project/topic]".
- Card schema: (see L5 earlier).
  - Fields: card_id, trigger_type, title, summary, linked_topic_id, priority, created_at, expires_at, signals[], evidence[], actions[], consumed.
- Expiry and eviction:
  - Default expiry = created_at + 48 hours. Expiry enforced by TTL in storage and cache.
  - Eviction logic:
    - If consumed (assistant acted on it), keep short audit entry but remove live card.
    - If priority low and no interaction in 12 hours, mark for early expiry.
    - If user deletes/clears cards manually, set profile_deletion_flag/consent for cards removed (no events kept).
- Merge strategy:
  - Cards are appended (no overwrite). If multiple cards reference same topic with overlapping evidence, they may be deduplicated by merging evidence and raising priority; deduplication done by deterministic rules (same linked_topic_id & time-window).

SECTION 3 — STORAGE & SERVING ARCHITECTURE
Constraints recap:
- Read P99 latency < 5ms for synchronous assistant requests.
- 10M users, ~2KB per profile => ~20GB derived profile data (plus overhead), easily fits in memory-backed caches.
- Writes are async / eventual.

Suggested stack (Azure-native equivalent since product is Microsoft Edge):
- Persistent store (source-of-truth):
  - Azure Cosmos DB (single-region write or multi-region with preferred region per user) or AWS DynamoDB equivalent.
  - Data model: per-user document (JSON) keyed by user_id (partition key). Schema versioned.
  - Rationale: scalable, low-latency single-digit-ms read in regional replica; supports TTL for L5 cards.
- Hot cache (read path):
  - Managed Redis Cluster (Azure Cache for Redis / Redis Enterprise) as read-through cache (primary sync read).
  - Cache key scheme: "profile:{user_id}" -> serialized JSON (L1-L5).
  - Keep profiles in Redis with TTL of e.g., 15 minutes; read-through ensures cache warmed at first read.
  - For P99 <5ms across global infra, deploy Redis clusters in the same region as the assistant service.
- Indexing / search:
  - Vector store / inverted index not required for profile retrieval; any topic search uses L3 clusters stored in profile or separate derived search index refreshed periodically.
- Synchronous read path (assistant request):
  1) Assistant server receives request with user_id.
  2) Read from Redis (GET profile:{user_id}). If HIT -> return profile JSON in-memory within <5ms.
  3) If MISS -> read from Cosmos DB (single-document read), write back to Redis, return. Cosmos reads aimed to be <10ms but miss rate limited by cache.
  4) Minimal transformation at read; assistant uses profile layers to personalize response. No raw event data included.
- Async write/update path (profile updates):
  - Event processing workers produce derived summaries and submit profile updates to an Update API:
    1) Worker publishes an "profile-update" message to a durable message queue (Azure Service Bus / Event Hubs / Kafka) with update delta and target user_id.
    2) Profile writer service consumes queue; applies merge logic, validates, writes to Cosmos DB (single document update). Writes should be idempotent (use operation_id).
    3) After DB write success, writer invalidates/updates Redis entry (push update to cache or remove cache key to force re-read). Cache invalidation must be eventual (synchronous invalidation not required).
  - For L5 cards: use DB TTL to auto-expire or writer removes on expiry.
- Caching strategy details:
  - Per-user Redis keys TTL 15 minutes.
  - Cache write-on-read (read-through) and writer pushes updated value after major updates (L1/L2/L3/L4/L5 changes) to reduce misses.
  - L5 cards: short TTL (48h), consider separate cache key "profile:{user_id}:cards" with more aggressive expiry on events.
  - Invalidation: On update, writer issues DEL profile:{user_id} OR updates it with new value. To avoid race conditions use small sequence number in profile and optimistic concurrency in DB writes.
- Scaling and performance:
  - 10M keys, average 2KB => ~20GB cached. Redis Enterprise cluster can support multiple shards; keep hot working set in memory.
  - Cosmos DB used as durable store with per-partition throughput scaled to expected write rates.
- Security:
  - Encryption at rest & in transit.
  - ACLs restricting profile read to assistant service with scoped tokens.
  - Audit logging for profile reads/writes; logs sanitized so they do not contain raw events.
- Deletion & user API:
  - Expose API for users to view profile (returns layers) and delete/clear (sets profile_deletion_flag, writes tombstone to DB and deletes Redis key). Deletion triggers asynchronous purge from DB within SLA (per GDPR) and removal of any derived backups.
  - When deletion request received, writer processes immediately with highest priority.

SECTION 4 — LLM SUMMARIZATION PIPELINE
Overview:
- Pipeline components:
  1) Event ingestor (client-side aggregator in Edge sends aggregated signals to server as ephemeral summaries — but zero raw data stored).
  2) Batcher: groups aggregated signal records per user and per time-window.
  3) Transformer pre-processors: non-LLM classifiers for topic candidate extraction, PII redaction checks, feature extraction.
  4) LLM summarizer(s): call to model(s) to produce JSON outputs for layers.
  5) Post-processing: JSON parsing, validation, confidence checks, schema validation.
  6) Profile writer: merges and writes to DB and cache.

Event batching:
- Raw events are aggregated on-device and/or immediately transformed into minimal derived tokens on client:
  - Edge will pre-aggregate by domain categories, counts, and timestamps (to respect zero raw-data rule).
- On server, events arriving for user are collected in per-user mini-batches:
  - L1: uses 30-day aggregated summary (batch window: 30d)
  - L2: weekly window
  - L3: sliding 7-day window with hourly micro-batches for spike detection
  - L4: last 24-72h window; real-time triggers for big changes
  - L5: near-realtime — event aggregator detects triggers and emits card creation jobs
- Batching parameters:
  - L3 nightly batch processes all user candidate signals from the last 24h.
  - For spikes: stream-processing detects threshold crossings and immediately emits a job.

Summarization model(s):
- Recommended approach: hybrid multi-model strategy for cost-quality tradeoff:
  - Frequent/cheap updates (L3, L4, L5): use a smaller fast model (e.g., 7B-13B parameter model served on optimized hardware) that is tuned/adapterized for summarization. This reduces cost and latency for high-volume updates.
  - Infrequent/high-importance updates (L1, complex L2 updates): use a larger high-quality model (e.g., 70B or LLM-optimized variant) for higher fidelity once/month.
  - All models are deployed on secure server-side infra (Azure ML / GPU clusters) with rate limiting and monitoring.
  - Use retrieval-augmented summarization: supply pre-computed topic candidates and counts as structured context to reduce hallucination.

Prompt structure — example full prompt for generating L3 (Interests) layer
(Plain-text example — the system sends structured JSON to LLM; LLM responds with strict JSON. Use system role to enforce schema.)

System instruction:
"You are a summarization assistant that converts aggregated behavioral signals into an 'Interests' JSON object. Never output narrative text — only JSON that strictly matches the schema provided. Do not invent PII. Use conservative inference; if signal is weak, set confidence low. Each cluster must include id, label, keywords (3-8), one example, score 0-1, last_activity ISO timestamp, decay_half_life_days."

User input (structured fields appended):
{
  "user_id":"user-xxxx",
  "window":"2026-04-06T00:00:00Z/2026-04-07T23:59:59Z",
  "aggregated_signals": {
    "domain_category_counts": { "ai/tech":12, "news/business":3, "automotive":4 },
    "search_topic_candidates": [ {"topic":"prompt engineering","score":0.88}, {"topic":"EV charging","score":0.45} ],
    "click_category_counts": { "ai/tech":8, "automotive":3 },
    "highlight_counts_by_topic": {"ai/tech":2}
  },
  "existing_clusters":[ ... up to top 5 ],
  "max_clusters":5
}

Assistant (expected output — strict JSON):

{
  "clusters":[
    { "id":"c1-<hash>", "label":"Generative AI","keywords":["LLM","prompt engineering","fine-tuning"], "examples":[{"url":"derived-domain:ai_blog","title":"Scaling LLMs","timestamp":"2026-04-07T19:01:00Z"}], "score":0.93, "last_activity":"2026-04-07T19:01:00Z", "decay_half_life_days":7 },
    { "id":"c2-<hash>", "label":"Electric Vehicles","keywords":["EV","charging","infrastructure"], "examples":[{"url":"derived-domain:news_auto","title":"New EV charging","timestamp":"2026-04-05T09:00:00Z"}], "score":0.45, "last_activity":"2026-04-05T09:00:00Z", "decay_half_life_days":14 }
  ],
  "global_confidence":0.87,
  "last_computed":"2026-04-07T20:00:00Z"
}

Output parsing and validation:
- Strict JSON schema validation (schema enforcement library). Reject outputs that fail schema.
- Additional checks:
  - Score bounds 0-1; timestamp ISO format.
  - Keywords are sanitized (no emails, phone numbers, or long passages).
  - Maximum cluster count enforced.
  - LLM output must include provenance hints (evidence counts) or else mark as low confidence.
- If parsing fails:
  - Retry with same model (1 retry) with instruction to "strictly output valid JSON only".
  - If still fails, fallback to non-LLM merge: use the non-LLM topic classifier's top-N candidates to update profile with low confidence and flag for human review.
- Validation also runs PII detector on outputs (NER + regexes). If any PII detected, redact and set confidence to 0 for that field and log for audit.

Failure handling:
- LLM call failure:
  - Retry once (exponential backoff).
  - If persistent, mark update as failed; leave existing profile unchanged and create a "stale" flag for the layer. Send metrics/alert to ops.
- LLM returns garbage (schema mismatch or hallucinated PII):
  - Reject response, attempt correction via re-prompt. If failure persists, fall back to heuristic update (merge using previous layer values and non-LLM classifier outputs).
- Partial outputs:
  - Accept partial updates if they pass validation and are higher confidence than existing values (e.g., new cluster added but no examples) — but mark missing fields and set layer quality_score lower.
- Auditing:
  - All LLM outputs stored temporarily for debugging only and purged per retention policy. No raw user event storage is kept.

SECTION 5 — EVALUATION FRAMEWORK
Goals: measure quality of profile layers and impact on assistant personalization while preserving privacy.

Offline evaluation
- Ground-truth datasets:
  - Curated, labeled set of users (opt-in research panel) mapping behavioral aggregates -> human-labeled interests/preferences/identity.
  - Synthetic user scenarios to test edge cases (e.g., multi-topic users).
- Offline metrics:
  - Precision/Recall on top-K interest clusters vs human labels.
  - Cluster-level F1, NMI (normalized mutual information) between predicted clusters and ground truth.
  - Calibration of confidence scores (expected calibration error).
  - Stability metrics: false positive flip-rate for L1 identity over time.
  - PII leakage tests: run detectors to ensure no PII introduced.
- Automated offline checks:
  - Sanity rules: e.g., "topics_to_avoid" should not exceed N items; scores in [0,1]; no direct PII strings.

Online evaluation (production)
- Behavioral metrics:
  - Assistant engagement lift: comparison of sessions with profile-enabled personalization vs control:
    - Task success rate (user completes prompted action).
    - Click-through and click-to-act rate for assistant suggestions.
    - Time-to-completion metrics (how quickly users get desired information).
  - User feedback:
    - Explicit ratings on assistant helpfulness when profile-driven suggestions used.
  - Content quality:
    - Reduced follow-up clarification rate (assistant needed fewer clarifying questions).
  - Profile health metrics:
    - Coverage: % of users with valid L3 clusters.
    - Freshness: median age of L3 update.
    - Conflict rate: instances where L2 contradicts L3 (flagged).
- Safety & privacy metrics:
  - PII-detection incidents (should be zero).
  - Deletion SLA compliance: % deletions completed within SLA window.
  - User opt-outs: % users disabling profile; reasons if provided.

A/B testing design
- Experiment: profile-enabled personalization (treatment) vs profile-disabled baseline (control).
- Population: production user traffic, randomization at user level, stratified by device/region.
- Primary metrics:
  - User-rated helpfulness (average rating),
  - Task completion rate,
  - Click-through on assistant suggestions.
- Secondary metrics:
  - Session length, retention (7-day retention), reduction in follow-ups.
- Safety guardrails:
  - Stop experiment if PII incidents > 0 or privacy opt-out rate spikes.
- Duration & power:
  - Run until statistical significance (pre-defined MDE) or 2–4 weeks.
- Additional variant:
  - Ablation test to measure contribution of each layer (e.g., L3-only vs L3+L4) to find which layers deliver the most lift.

Privacy compliance checks
- Zero raw behavioral data stored: enforce at client-side and ingestion layer that only derived/aggregated signals are transmitted. Implement ingestion-side validator that rejects payloads containing raw page content, full URLs beyond domain categorization, or raw search queries unless explicitly consented.
- PII detection:
  - Always run regex & named-entity recognition over LLM outputs before persisting. If PII found, redact and log an incident for ops/DS.
- Consent & controls:
  - Per-user consent flags controlling which layers are enabled. Default to opt-out for identity inference (L1) if no explicit consent.
- Right to delete:
  - Immediate API path to delete profile; writer removes document and cache, and triggers purge of derived backups.
- Data minimization:
  - Persist minimal evidence (domain names, small titles), avoid full-text storage.
- Auditing:
  - Periodic privacy audits, and access logs for who/what service read profiles.
- Explainability:
  - Provide a "Why this suggestion?" feature where the assistant shows which layer and evidence phrases led to the suggestion (e.g., "Because you recently opened articles about X").

Open Questions and Tradeoffs
- Where to perform aggregation and how much to aggregate client-side vs server-side?
  - Tradeoff: more client-side aggregation better for privacy but increases on-device complexity. Recommend client pre-aggregation into categorical counts and hash-based topic tokens.
- LLM model selection and costs:
  - Tradeoff: larger models give better accuracy (L1) but cost more. Use hybrid approach; tune thresholds for using large models only when necessary.
- Freshness vs stability:
  - L4 and L5 should be fresh; L1 must be stable. Tuning decay_half_life and merge thresholds is empirical and needs A/B tests.
- PII leakage prevention:
  - LLM hallucination risk remains. Must enforce strict schema & post-processing PII detectors and have failsafe fallbacks.
- Explainability vs brevity:
  - Showing reasons to users improves transparency but may reveal derived signals. Provide sanitized explanations that do not reveal specific visited URLs.
- Storage compliance:
  - Although derived data is OK to store, some jurisdictions may treat certain derived inference as personal data. Ensure legal review and per-region policy differences.

Appendix — Example flow (end-to-end)
1) Edge aggregates last-24h signals into a derived payload (domain counts, topic tokens) and sends to server.
2) Spike detector sees 6 queries on "prompt engineering" in 40 minutes -> emits L5 card job.
3) L5 card created, stored in profile and cached. Assistant reads profile (cache HIT) and surfaces a proactive suggestion: "Would you like a 3-slide summary on prompt engineering?" with "Why?" button that shows sanitized evidence (e.g., "Recent searches and opened tutorials").
4) The nightly L3 job runs: server batches user signals, calls small LLM, gets clusters, validates, and merges with existing L3. Writer updates DB and invalidates cache.

Summary
- This design provides a 5-layer, schema-driven profile that balances freshness and stability; uses LLM summarization with strict JSON schema enforcement and multi-model cost/quality strategy; uses Redis + Cosmos DB for P99 <5ms reads and async, reliable writes; enforces privacy-by-design (no raw behavioral data persisted) and supports deletion and auditability; and defines concrete evaluation metrics and triggers for transient Interest Cards.
